sanskrit: brahmadaṇḍasamasparśā vajravegā durāsadāḥ mama prāṇān ārujanti neme bāṇāḥ śikhaṇḍinaḥ
english: "Their touch is like the rod of Brahmā, their force like the thunderbolt, and they are not to be withstood; they tear at my very life-breath. These are no arrows of Śikhaṇḍin."

sanskrit: bhujagā iva saṃkruddhā lelihānā viṣolbaṇāḥ mamāviśanti marmāṇi neme bāṇāḥ śikhaṇḍinaḥ
english: "Like enraged serpents, tongues flickering, swollen with venom, they enter into my vital parts. These are no arrows of Śikhaṇḍin."

sanskrit: nāśayantīva me prāṇān yamadūtā ivāhitāḥ gadāparighasaṃsparśā neme bāṇāḥ śikhaṇḍinaḥ
english: "They destroy my life-breath like the hostile messengers of Yama; their touch is like that of mace and iron club. These are no arrows of Śikhaṇḍin."

sanskrit: kṛntanti mama gātrāṇi māghamāse gavām iva arjunasya ime bāṇā neme bāṇāḥ śikhaṇḍinaḥ
english: "They cut into my limbs as the cold cuts into cattle in the month of Māgha. These are the arrows of Arjuna; they are no arrows of Śikhaṇḍin."

sanskrit: sarve hy api na me duḥkhaṃ kuryur anye narādhipāḥ vīraṃ gaṇḍīvadhanvānam ṛte jiṣṇuṃ kapidhvajam
english: "All the other kings together could not bring me such pain—none but that hero, the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva, victorious Jiṣṇu of the ape-bannered car."

sanskrit: iti bruvañ śāṃtanavo didhakṣur iva pāṇḍavam saviṣphuliṅgāṃ dīptāgrāṃ śaktiṃ cikṣepa bhārata
english: So speaking, the son of Śāntanu, as though he would burn the Pāṇḍava to ashes, hurled a spear that scattered sparks and blazed at its point, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: tām asya viśikhaiś chittvā tridhā tribhir apātayat paśyatāṃ kuruvīrāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ tatra bhārata
english: But Arjuna, cutting it with three shafts into three pieces, brought it down before the eyes of all the Kuru heroes there, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: carmāthādatta gāṅgeyo jātarūpapariṣkṛtam khaḍgaṃ cānyataraṃ prepsur mṛtyor agre jayāya vā
english: Then the son of Gaṅgā took up a shield adorned with gold and a sword as well, resolved either upon death or upon victory at its threshold.

sanskrit: tasya tac chatadhā carma vyadhamad daṃśitātmanaḥ rathād anavarūḍhasya tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: But Arjuna shattered that shield of the armored warrior into a hundred fragments while he had not yet descended from his car; and that was a thing of wonder.

sanskrit: vinadyoccaiḥ siṃha iva svāny anīkāny acodayat abhidravata gāṅgeyaṃ māṃ vo 'stu bhayam aṇv api
english: Roaring aloud like a lion, Bhīṣma urged on his own troops: "Rush upon the son of Gaṅgā! Let not even the smallest fear possess you for my sake!"

sanskrit: atha te tomaraiḥ prāsair bāṇaughaiś ca samantataḥ paṭṭiśaiś ca sanistriṃśair nānāpraharaṇais tathā
english: Then on every side, with javelins, with lances, with floods of arrows, with battle-axes and swords and weapons of every kind,

sanskrit: vatsadantaiś ca bhallaiś ca tam ekam abhidudruvuḥ siṃhanādas tato ghoraḥ pāṇḍavānām ajāyata
english: with calf-tooth darts and broad-headed shafts, they all rushed upon him alone; and a terrible lion-roar arose then from the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tathaiva tava putrāś ca rājan bhīṣmajayaiṣiṇaḥ tam ekam abhyavartanta siṃhanādāṃś ca nedire
english: And likewise your sons, O king, longing for Bhīṣma's victory, closed about that one man and raised their lion-roars.

sanskrit: tatrāsīt tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ tāvakānāṃ paraiḥ saha daśame 'hani rājendra bhīṣmārjunasamāgame
english: There a tumultuous battle arose between your men and the foe, O lord of kings, on the tenth day, in the encounter of Bhīṣma and Arjuna.

sanskrit: āsīd gāṅga ivāvarto muhūrtam udadher iva sainyānāṃ yudhyamānānāṃ nighnatām itaretaram
english: For a moment it was like the whirlpool of the Gaṅgā, like that of the ocean, among the warring armies as they struck one another down.

sanskrit: agamyarūpā pṛthivī śoṇitāktā tadābhavat samaṃ ca viṣamaṃ caiva na prājñāyata kiṃ cana
english: The earth, drenched with blood, became impassable in appearance, and one could no longer tell level ground from broken.

sanskrit: yodhānām ayutaṃ hatvā tasmin sa daśame 'hani atiṣṭhad āhave bhīṣmo bhidyamāneṣu marmasu
english: Having slain ten thousand warriors on that tenth day, Bhīṣma stood firm in battle, though his vital parts were being pierced through.

sanskrit: tataḥ senāmukhe tasmin sthitaḥ pārtho dhanaṃjayaḥ madhyena kurusainyānāṃ drāvayām āsa vāhinīm
english: Then, stationed at the head of that host, Pārtha Dhanaṃjaya drove the army into rout through the midst of the Kuru ranks.

sanskrit: vayaṃ śvetahayād bhītāḥ kuntīputrād dhanaṃjayāt pīḍyamānāḥ śitaiḥ śastraiḥ pradravāma mahāraṇāt
english: We, terrified of him of the white horses, Dhanaṃjaya the son of Kuntī, sorely pressed by his keen weapons, fled from the great battle.

sanskrit: sauvīrāḥ kitavāḥ prācyāḥ pratīcyodīcyamālavāḥ abhīṣāhāḥ śūrasenāḥ śibayo 'tha vasātayaḥ
english: The Sauvīras, the Kitavas, the men of the East, the West, and the North, the Mālavas, the Abhīṣāhas, the Śūrasenas, the Śibis, and the Vasātis,

sanskrit: śālvāśrayās trigartāś ca ambaṣṭhāḥ kekayaiḥ saha dvādaśaite janapadāḥ śarārtā vraṇapīḍitāḥ saṃgrāme na jahur bhīṣmaṃ yudhyamānaṃ kirīṭinā
english: the dependents of the Śālvas, the Trigartas, the Ambaṣṭhas together with the Kekayas—these twelve peoples, though tormented by arrows and afflicted with wounds, did not in that battle forsake Bhīṣma as he fought with Arjuna the diademed.

sanskrit: tatas tam ekaṃ bahavaḥ parivārya samantataḥ parikālya kurūn sarvāñ śaravarṣair avākiran
english: Then the many, surrounding that one man on every side and driving back all the Kurus, overwhelmed him with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: nipātayata gṛhṇīta vidhyatātha ca karṣata ity āsīt tumulaḥ śabdo rājan bhīṣmarathaṃ prati
english: "Strike him down! Seize him! Pierce him! Drag him out!"—such was the tumultuous outcry, O king, around the chariot of Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: abhihatya śaraughais taṃ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ na tasyāsīd anirbhinnaṃ gātreṣv aṅgulamātrakam
english: Smitten by floods of arrows by the hundreds and the thousands, there was not upon his body so much as a finger's breadth left unpierced.

sanskrit: evaṃ vibho tava pitā śarair viśakalīkṛtaḥ śitāgraiḥ phalgunenājau prākśirāḥ prāpatad rathāt kiṃciccheṣe dinakare putrāṇāṃ tava paśyatām
english: Thus, O lord, your father, his body torn to pieces by the keen-pointed shafts of Phalguna, fell from his chariot in battle, his head toward the east, while a little of the day yet remained, before the eyes of your sons.

sanskrit: hā heti divi devānāṃ pārthivānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ patamāne rathād bhīṣme babhūva sumahān svanaḥ
english: "Alas! Alas!"—a mighty cry arose on every side, from the gods in heaven and from the kings on earth, as Bhīṣma fell from his car.

sanskrit: taṃ patantam abhiprekṣya mahātmānaṃ pitāmaham saha bhīṣmeṇa sarveṣāṃ prāpatan hṛdayāni naḥ
english: Beholding that great-souled grandsire fall, the hearts of us all fell down together with Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: sa papāta mahābāhur vasudhām anunādayan indradhvaja ivotsṛṣṭaḥ ketuḥ sarvadhanuṣmatām dharaṇīṃ nāspṛśac cāpi śarasaṃghaiḥ samācitaḥ
english: The mighty-armed one fell, making the earth resound, like the banner of Indra let loose—he, the ensign of all the bowmen; yet, thickly studded with masses of arrows, he did not touch the ground.

sanskrit: śaratalpe maheṣvāsaṃ śayānaṃ puruṣarṣabham rathāt prapatitaṃ cainaṃ divyo bhāvaḥ samāviśat
english: As that bull among men, the great archer, lay fallen from his car upon a bed of arrows, a divine presence entered into him.

sanskrit: abhyavarṣata parjanyaḥ prākampata ca medinī patan sa dadṛśe cāpi kharvitaṃ ca divākaram
english: The rain-cloud poured down and the earth trembled; and as he fell he saw the sun shrunken in its course.

sanskrit: saṃjñāṃ caivālabhad vīraḥ kālaṃ saṃcintya bhārata antarikṣe ca śuśrāva divyāṃ vācaṃ samantataḥ
english: The hero regained his consciousness, reflecting upon the time, O descendant of Bharata, and he heard from the sky a divine voice on every side.

sanskrit: kathaṃ mahātmā gāṅgeyaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ kālaṃ kartā naravyāghraḥ saṃprāpte dakṣiṇāyane
english: "How shall the great-souled son of Gaṅgā, foremost of all who bear arms, that tiger among men, meet his end now that the sun's southward course has come?"

sanskrit: sthito 'smīti ca gāṅgeyas tac chrutvā vākyam abravīt dhārayām āsa ca prāṇān patito 'pi hi bhūtale uttarāyaṇam anvicchan bhīṣmaḥ kurupitāmahaḥ
english: Hearing that utterance, the son of Gaṅgā answered, "I yet abide," and held fast his life-breaths, though fallen upon the ground—Bhīṣma, grandsire of the Kurus, awaiting the sun's northward turning.

sanskrit: tasya tan matam ājñāya gaṅgā himavataḥ sutā maharṣīn haṃsarūpeṇa preṣayām āsa tatra vai
english: Knowing that resolve of his, Gaṅgā, daughter of Himavat, sent thither great sages in the form of swans.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃpātino haṃsās tvaritā mānasaukasaḥ ājagmuḥ sahitā draṣṭuṃ bhīṣmaṃ kurupitāmaham yatra śete naraśreṣṭhaḥ śaratalpe pitāmahaḥ
english: Then the swift swans, dwellers of Lake Mānasa, came flying together to see Bhīṣma, grandsire of the Kurus, there where that best of men, the grandsire, lay upon his bed of arrows.

sanskrit: te tu bhīṣmaṃ samāsādya munayo haṃsarūpiṇaḥ apaśyañ śaratalpasthaṃ bhīṣmaṃ kurupitāmaham
english: And those sages in the guise of swans, drawing near to Bhīṣma, beheld him, the grandsire of the Kurus, lying upon his bed of arrows.

sanskrit: te taṃ dṛṣṭvā mahātmānaṃ kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam gāṅgeyaṃ bharataśreṣṭhaṃ dakṣiṇena ca bhāskaram
english: Seeing that great-souled son of Gaṅgā, foremost of the Bharatas, and making their reverent circuit about him, with the sun upon their right,

sanskrit: itaretaram āmantrya prāhus tatra manīṣiṇaḥ bhīṣma eva mahātmā san saṃsthātā dakṣiṇāyane
english: those wise ones, taking counsel one with another, said there: "Bhīṣma, great-souled as he is, would yet make his end while the sun runs its southward course!"

sanskrit: ity uktvā prasthitān haṃsān dakṣiṇām abhito diśam saṃprekṣya vai mahābuddhiś cintayitvā ca bhārata
english: Having so spoken, the swans set forth toward the southern quarter; and the deeply wise one, gazing after them and reflecting, O descendant of Bharata,

sanskrit: tān abravīc chāṃtanavo nāhaṃ gantā kathaṃ cana dakṣiṇāvṛtta āditye etan me manasi sthitam
english: the son of Śāntanu said to them: "By no means shall I depart while the sun is turned to the south. This is settled in my mind."

sanskrit: gamiṣyāmi svakaṃ sthānam āsīd yan me purātanam udagāvṛtta āditye haṃsāḥ satyaṃ bravīmi vaḥ
english: "I shall go to my own abode that was mine of old when the sun has turned to the north. O swans, I tell you the truth."

sanskrit: dhārayiṣyāmy ahaṃ prāṇān uttarāyaṇakāṅkṣayā aiśvaryabhūtaḥ prāṇānām utsarge niyato hy aham tasmāt prāṇān dhārayiṣye mumūrṣur udagāyane
english: "I shall hold fast my life-breaths in longing for the northward course, for I am master over the laying down of those breaths, fixed in my purpose. Therefore I shall hold them, ready to die when the sun moves northward."

sanskrit: yaś ca datto varo mahyaṃ pitrā tena mahātmanā chandato mṛtyur ity evaṃ tasya cāstu varas tathā
english: "And the boon that was granted me by that great-souled father of mine—that death should come at my own will—let that boon of his stand fulfilled."

sanskrit: dhārayiṣye tataḥ prāṇān utsarge niyate sati ity uktvā tāṃs tadā haṃsān aśeta śaratalpagaḥ
english: "I shall hold my breaths until the appointed hour for their release." Having so spoken to those swans, he lay there upon his bed of arrows.

sanskrit: evaṃ kurūṇāṃ patite śṛṅge bhīṣme mahaujasi pāṇḍavāḥ sṛñjayāś caiva siṃhanādaṃ pracakrire
english: When Bhīṣma of mighty splendor, the very summit of the Kurus, had thus fallen, the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas raised their lion-roar.

sanskrit: tasmin hate mahāsattve bharatānām amadhyame na kiṃ cit pratyapadyanta putrās te bharatarṣabha saṃmohaś caiva tumulaḥ kurūṇām abhavat tadā
english: When that one of great courage, peerless among the Bharatas, had been slain, your sons knew not what to do, O bull of the Bharatas, and a tumultuous bewilderment fell then upon the Kurus.

sanskrit: nṛpā duryodhanamukhā niḥśvasya rurudus tataḥ viṣādāc ca ciraṃ kālam atiṣṭhan vigatendriyāḥ
english: The kings, with Duryodhana at their head, sighed and then wept, and out of grief stood for a long while as though robbed of their senses.

sanskrit: dadhyuś caiva mahārāja na yuddhe dadhire manaḥ ūrugrāhagṛhītāś ca nābhyadhāvanta pāṇḍavān
english: They brooded, O great king, and set not their minds upon the fight; and seized as if by cramp in the thighs, they did not rush upon the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: avadhye śaṃtanoḥ putre hate bhīṣme mahaujasi abhāvaḥ sumahān rājan kurūn āgād atandritaḥ
english: When the son of Śaṃtanu, deemed unslayable, the splendid Bhīṣma, had been slain, a vast and unrelenting ruin came upon the Kurus, O king.

sanskrit: hatapravīrāś ca vayaṃ nikṛttāś ca śitaiḥ śaraiḥ kartavyaṃ nābhijānīmo nirjitāḥ savyasācinā
english: Our champions slain, ourselves cut down by keen arrows, vanquished by Savyasācin, we knew not what was to be done.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavās tu jayaṃ labdhvā paratra ca parāṃ gatim sarve dadhmur mahāśaṅkhāñ śūrāḥ parighabāhavaḥ somakāś ca sapañcālāḥ prāhṛṣyanta janeśvara
english: But the Pāṇḍavas, having won the victory and the supreme goal in the world beyond, those heroes with arms like iron bars all blew their great conches; and the Somakas with the Pāñcālas rejoiced greatly, O lord of men.

sanskrit: tatas tūryasahasreṣu nadatsu sumahābalaḥ āsphoṭayām āsa bhṛśaṃ bhīmaseno nanarta ca
english: Then, while a thousand trumpets sounded, the mighty Bhīmasena slapped his arms loudly and danced for joy.

sanskrit: senayor ubhayoś cāpi gāṅgeye vinipātite saṃnyasya vīrāḥ śastrāṇi prādhyāyanta samantataḥ
english: When the son of Gaṅgā had been brought down, the heroes of both armies laid aside their weapons and gave themselves up to reflection on every side.

sanskrit: prākrośan prāpataṃś cānye jagmur mohaṃ tathāpare kṣatraṃ cānye 'bhyanindanta bhīṣmaṃ caike 'bhyapūjayan
english: Some cried aloud, others fell down, and still others swooned away; some reviled the warrior order, while others did honor to Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaḥ pitaraś caiva praśaśaṃsur mahāvratam bharatānāṃ ca ye pūrve te cainaṃ praśaśaṃsire
english: The seers and the ancestors praised him of the great vow; and those who were the forefathers of the Bharatas, they too praised him.

sanskrit: mahopaniṣadaṃ caiva yogam āsthāya vīryavān japañ śāṃtanavo dhīmān kālākāṅkṣī sthito 'bhavat
english: And taking his stand upon the great secret doctrine and upon yoga, the valiant and wise son of Śāntanu remained murmuring his prayers, awaiting his hour.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca katham āsaṃs tadā yodhā hīnā bhīṣmeṇa saṃjaya balinā devakalpena gurvarthe brahmacāriṇā
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: How fared the warriors then, O Saṃjaya, bereft of Bhīṣma—the mighty one, godlike, who kept his celibate vow for his elder's sake?

sanskrit: tadaiva nihatān manye kurūn anyāṃś ca pārthivān na prāharad yadā bhīṣmo ghṛṇitvād drupadātmaje
english: I count the Kurus and the other kings as slain already from that moment when Bhīṣma, out of compassion, would not strike at the son of Drupada.

sanskrit: tato duḥkhataraṃ manye kim anyat prabhaviṣyati yad adya pitaraṃ śrutvā nihataṃ mama durmateḥ
english: What grief could ever befall worse than this, when today I hear that my father has been slain—I, the evil-minded one?

sanskrit: aśmasāramayaṃ nūnaṃ hṛdayaṃ mama saṃjaya śrutvā vinihataṃ bhīṣmaṃ śatadhā yan na dīryate
english: Surely my heart is made of iron, O Saṃjaya, that, hearing of Bhīṣma's slaying, it does not break asunder into a hundred pieces.

sanskrit: punaḥ punar na mṛṣyāmi hataṃ devavrataṃ raṇe na hato jāmadagnyena divyair astraiḥ sma yaḥ purā
english: Again and again I cannot endure it—that Devavrata has been slain in battle, he whom of old not even the son of Jamadagni could slay with his celestial weapons.

sanskrit: yad adya nihatenājau bhīṣmeṇa jayam icchatā ceṣṭitaṃ narasiṃhena tan me kathaya saṃjaya
english: Tell me, O Saṃjaya, what that lion among men, Bhīṣma, did in his desire for victory before he was slain in battle this day.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sāyāhne nyapatad bhūmau dhārtarāṣṭrān viṣādayan pāñcālānāṃ dadad dharṣaṃ kuruvṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: At the close of day the aged grandsire of the Kurus fell to the earth, plunging the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra into despair and giving joy to the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: sa śete śaratalpastho medinīm aspṛśaṃs tadā bhīṣmo rathāt prapatitaḥ pracyuto dharaṇītale
english: He lay upon his bed of arrows, not touching the earth, Bhīṣma, fallen from his car, cast down upon the ground.

sanskrit: hā heti tumulaḥ śabdo bhūtānāṃ samapadyata sīmāvṛkṣe nipatite kurūṇāṃ samitikṣaye
english: "Alas! Alas!"—a tumultuous cry went up from all beings when the boundary-tree of the Kurus fell at the breaking of their host.

sanskrit: ubhayoḥ senayo rājan kṣatriyān bhayam āviśat bhīṣmaṃ śaṃtanavaṃ dṛṣṭvā viśīrṇakavacadhvajam kuravaḥ paryavartanta pāṇḍavāś ca viśāṃ pate
english: Fear came upon the warriors of both armies, O king; seeing Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, with shattered armor and standard, the Kurus turned about, and the Pāṇḍavas as well, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: khaṃ tamovṛtam āsīc ca nāsīd bhānumataḥ prabhā rarāsa pṛthivī caiva bhīṣme śāṃtanave hate
english: The sky was wrapped in darkness, and the radiance of the sun was no more, and the earth itself groaned aloud when Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, was slain.

sanskrit: ayaṃ brahmavidāṃ śreṣṭho ayaṃ brahmavidāṃ gatiḥ ity abhāṣanta bhūtāni śayānaṃ bharatarṣabham
english: "This is the foremost of the knowers of Brahman; this is the refuge of the knowers of Brahman"—so the beings spoke of that bull of the Bharatas as he lay there.

sanskrit: ayaṃ pitaram ājñāya kāmārtaṃ śaṃtanuṃ purā ūrdhvaretasam ātmānaṃ cakāra puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: "This bull among men, knowing of old that his father Śaṃtanu was tormented by desire, made of himself one whose seed was drawn upward in chastity."

sanskrit: iti sma śaratalpasthaṃ bharatānām amadhyamam ṛṣayaḥ paryadhāvanta sahitāḥ siddhacāraṇaiḥ
english: Thus the seers, together with the Siddhas and Cāraṇas, hastened about him, the peerless one of the Bharatas, as he lay upon his bed of arrows.

sanskrit: hate śāṃtanave bhīṣme bharatānāṃ pitāmahe na kiṃ cit pratyapadyanta putrās tava ca bhārata
english: When Bhīṣma, son of Śāntanu, grandsire of the Bharatas, was slain, your sons knew not what to do, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: vivarṇavadanāś cāsan gataśrīkāś ca bhārata atiṣṭhan vrīḍitāś caiva hriyā yuktā hy adhomukhāḥ
english: Their faces grew pale and their splendor departed, O descendant of Bharata; they stood abashed, overcome with shame, their faces bent downward.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś ca jayaṃ labdhvā saṃgrāmaśirasi sthitāḥ sarve dadhmur mahāśaṅkhān hemajālapariṣkṛtān
english: But the Pāṇḍavas, having won the victory and standing at the forefront of the battle, all blew their great conches adorned with nets of gold.

sanskrit: bhṛśaṃ tūryaninādeṣu vādyamāneṣu cānagha apaśyāma raṇe rājan bhīmasenaṃ mahābalam ākrīḍamānaṃ kaunteyaṃ harṣeṇa mahatā yutam
english: And while the trumpets were loudly sounding, O sinless one, we saw in the battle, O king, the mighty Bhīmasena, son of Kuntī, sporting and filled with exceeding joy.

sanskrit: nihatya samare śatrūn mahābalasamanvitān saṃmohaś cāpi tumulaḥ kurūṇām abhavat tadā
english: Having slain in battle his foes endowed with great strength—and a tumultuous bewilderment then fell upon the Kurus.

sanskrit: karṇaduryodhanau cāpi niḥśvasetāṃ muhur muhuḥ tathā nipatite bhīṣme kauravāṇāṃ dhuraṃdhare hāhākāram abhūt sarvaṃ nirmaryādam avartata
english: Karṇa and Duryodhana too sighed again and again; and when Bhīṣma, the chief upholder of the Kauravas, had thus fallen, all became a cry of woe, and everything passed beyond restraint.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca patitaṃ bhīṣmaṃ putro duḥśāsanas tava uttamaṃ javam āsthāya droṇānīkaṃ samādravat
english: And seeing Bhīṣma fallen, your son Duḥśāsana, taking on the utmost speed, rushed toward the division of Droṇa.

sanskrit: bhrātrā prasthāpito vīraḥ svenānīkena daṃśitaḥ prayayau puruṣavyāghraḥ svasainyam abhicodayan
english: Sent forth by his brother, that hero, mailed and amid his own host, that tiger among men advanced, urging on his troops.

sanskrit: tam āyāntam abhiprekṣya kuravaḥ paryavārayan duḥśāsanaṃ mahārāja kim ayaṃ vakṣyatīti vai
english: Beholding him approach, the Kurus gathered round Duḥśāsana, O great king, wondering, "What will he have to say?"

sanskrit: tato droṇāya nihataṃ bhīṣmam ācaṣṭa kauravaḥ droṇas tad apriyaṃ śrutvā sahasā nyapatad rathāt
english: Then the Kaurava announced to Droṇa that Bhīṣma had been slain; and Droṇa, hearing those unwelcome tidings, fell at once from his chariot.
